arxiv-2207-11826.title: Coupled charge and energy transfer dynamics in light harvesting complexes from a hybrid hierarchical equations of motion approach
arxiv-2207-11826.creator: Thomas P. Fay, David T. Limmer
arxiv-2207-11826.description: Abstract We describe a method for simulating exciton dynamics in protein-pigment complexes, including effects from charge transfer as well as fluorescence. The method combines the hierarchical equations of motion, which are used to describe quantum dynamics of excitons, and the Nakajima-Zwanzig quantum master equation, which is used to describe slower charge transfer processes.

arxiv-2208-02968.title: A Case-Study of Sample-Based Bayesian Forecasting Algorithms
arxiv-2208-02968.creator: Taylor R. Brown
arxiv-2208-02968.description: Abstract For a Bayesian, real-time forecasting with the posterior predictive distribution can be challenging for a variety of time series models. First, estimating the parameters of a time series model can be difficult with sample-based approaches when the model’s likelihood is intractable and/or when the data set being used is large.

arxiv-2208-13719.title: The general Two-Higgs Doublet Model in a gauge-invariant form
arxiv-2208-13719.creator: L. Sartore, M. Maniatis, I. Schienbein, B. Herrmann
arxiv-2208-13719.description: Abstract In the general Two-Higgs Doublet Model it has been shown that the Higgs potential can be expressed in terms of gauge-independent quantities. In particular, stability, electroweak symmetry breaking, and CP symmetry can be understood in a concise way, avoiding unphysical gauge degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2305-13081.title: An FFT-based framework for predicting corrosion-driven damage in fractal porous media
arxiv-2305-13081.creator: Mohit Pundir, David S. Kammer, Ueli Angst
arxiv-2305-13081.description: Abstract Understanding fracture in cementitious materials caused by the deposition and growth of corrosion products requires scale-bridging approaches due to the large length-scale difference between the micro-pores, where deposition occurs, and the structure, where deterioration manifests. Cementitious materials bear a highly heterogeneous micro-structure owing to the fractal nature of micro-pores.

arxiv-2311-18667.title: Topological nodal line semimetals with chiral symmetry
arxiv-2311-18667.creator: Faruk Abdulla, Ganpathy Murthy, Ankur Das
arxiv-2311-18667.description: Abstract Topological semimetals in three dimensions display band-touchings at points (Weyl or Dirac semimetals) or nodal lines in the Brillouin zone. Weyl semimetals can occur with internal symmetries only (time-reversal 𝒯 {\cal T} , charge conjugation 𝒞 {\cal C} , and a product of the two, called chiral/sublattice symmetry 𝒮 = 𝒯𝒞 {\cal S}={\cal T}{\cal C} ).

arxiv-2402-17647.title: A Spectropolarimetric Study of Pictor A Radio Galaxy with MeerKAT 2023 A Spectropolarimetric Study of Pictor A Radio Galaxy with MeerKAT – 15
arxiv-2402-17647.creator: Lexy A. L. Andati, Lerato M. Baidoo, Athanaseus J. T. Ramaila, Oleg M. Smirnov, Sphesihle Makhathini, Richard A. Perley
arxiv-2402-17647.description: Abstract We present the results of a polarimetric study from our new high-sensitivity L-band (0.8–1.7 GHz) observation of Pictor A with the MeerKAT radio telescope. We confirm the presence of the radio jet extending from the nucleus to the western hotspot of this source.

arxiv-2412-19570.title: Quantum K-theory and Integrability
arxiv-2412-19570.creator: Peter Koroteev
arxiv-2412-19570.description: Abstract . In this note, we explore some recent advancements in enumerative algebraic geometry, focusing particularly on the role of quantum K-theory of quiver varieties as viewed through the lens of integrable systems. We highlight a number of conjectures and open questions.

arxiv-2501-04623.title: Large-scale Grid Optimization: The Workhorse of Future Grid Computations Thanks:
arxiv-2501-04623.creator: Amritanshu Pandey and Mads R. Almassalkhi and Samuel Chevalier
arxiv-2501-04623.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amritanshu Pandey and Mads R. Almassalkhi and Samuel Chevalier. Purpose: The computation methods for modeling, controlling and optimizing the transforming grid are evolving rapidly. We review and systemize knowledge for a special class of computation methods that solve large-scale power grid optimization problems.

arxiv-2502-18856.title: Spectroastrometry and Reverberation Mapping of Active Galactic Nuclei. II. Measuring Geometric Distances and Black Hole Masses of Four Nearby Quasars
arxiv-2502-18856.creator: Yan-Rong Li, Jinyi Shangguan, Jian-Min Wang, Ric Davies, Daryl J. D. Santos, Frank Eisenhauer, Yu-Yang Songsheng, Hartmut Winkler, Jesús Aceituno, Hua-Rui Bai, Jin-Ming Bai, Michael S. Brotherton, Yixian Cao, Yong-Jie Chen, Pu Du, Feng-Na Fang, Jia-Qi Feng, Helmut Feuchtgruber, Natascha M. Förster S
arxiv-2502-18856.description: Abstract The geometric distances of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) are challenging to measure because of their exceptionally compact structure yet vast cosmic distances. A combination of spectroastrometry and reverberation mapping (SARM) of broad-line regions (BLRs) constitutes a novel means to probe the geometric distance of AGNs, which has recently become practically feasible owing to successful interferometric observations with VLTI/GRAVITY.

arxiv-2504-11660.title: On the packing dimension of distance sets with respect to 𝑪 \bm{C^{1\!}} and polyhedral norms Thanks: B. W. is supported by NSF CAREER Fellowship, DMS 2142064.
arxiv-2504-11660.creator: Iqra Altaf, Ryan Bushling, Bobby Wilson
arxiv-2504-11660.description: Abstract . We prove that, for every polyhedral or C 1 C^{1} norm on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} and every set E ⊆ ℝ d E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d} of packing dimension s s , the packing dimension of the distance set of E E with respect to that norm is at least s d \tfrac{s}{d} .

arxiv-2505-07613.title: Unveiling Phonon Contributions to Thermal Transport and the Failure of the Wiedemann-Franz Law in Ruthenium and Tungsten Thin Films
arxiv-2505-07613.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Thermal transport in nanoscale interconnects is dominated by intricate electron–phonon interactions and microstructural influences. As copper faces limitations at the nanoscale, tungsten and ruthenium have emerged as promising alternatives due to their substantial phonon contributions to thermal conductivity. Metals with stronger phonon-mediated thermal transport are particularly advantageous in nanoscale architectures, where phonons are less sensitive to size effects than electrons.

Sandstrom, Angela Adamo, Francesca Annibali, Daniela Calzetti, B. T. Draine, Svea Hernandez, Alec S. Hirschauer, Margaret Meixner, Dimitra Ri
arxiv-2507-12222.description: Abstract We present observations of the nearby extremely metal-poor galaxy I Zw 18 using the Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) and the JWST Mid-InfraRed Instrument (MIRI) Integral Field Spectrographs (IFS). From optical and mid-IR oxygen emission lines, we measured direct-method abundances for three ionic states of oxygen, including O 3+ /H + .

arxiv-2508-10995.title: Improving Text Style Transfer using Masked Diffusion Language Models with Inference-time Scaling
arxiv-2508-10995.creator: Tejomay Kishor Padole, Suyash P. Awate, Pushpak Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2508-10995.description: Abstract Masked diffusion language models (MDMs) have recently gained traction as a viable generative framework for natural language. This can be attributed to its scalability and ease of training compared to other diffusion model paradigms for discrete data, establishing itself as the state-of-the-art non-autoregressive generator for discrete data.

arxiv-2509-14547.title: (P)rior(D)yna(F)low: A Priori Dynamic Workflow Construction via Multi-Agent Collaboration
arxiv-2509-14547.creator: Yi Lin, Lujin Zhao, Yijie Shi
arxiv-2509-14547.description: Abstract Recent studies have shown that carefully designed workflows coordinating large language models (LLMs) significantly enhance task-solving capabilities compared to using a single model. While an increasing number of works focus on autonomous workflow construction, most existing approaches rely solely on historical experience, leading to limitations in efficiency and adaptability.

arxiv-2512-04296.title: GRASP : GR ouped A ctivation S hared P arameterization for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Robust Inference of Transformers
arxiv-2512-04296.creator: Malyaban Bal, Abhronil Sengupta
arxiv-2512-04296.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Malyaban Bal, Abhronil Sengupta. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) provides a scalable alternative to full-model adaptation by updating only a small subset of parameters in large pre-trained models. We introduce GRASP — GR ouped A ctivation S hared P arameterization — a lightweight PEFT framework that partitions the D D -dimensional token representations of selected layers into K ≪ D K\ll D groups and learns a shared scaling and shifting vector for each group.

pmc-10665145.title: Evaluating the zoonotic potential of RNA viromes of rodents provides new insight into rodent-borne zoonotic pathogens in Guangdong, China
pmc-10665145.creator: Boyang Yi, Qiang Deng, Cheng Guo, Xiaokang Li, Qin Wu, Renyun Zha, Xianhua Wang, Jiahai Lu
pmc-10665145.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases have been on the rise, with a significant proportion being zoonotic. Rodents, as the natural reservoirs of numerous diverse zoonotic viruses, pose a substantial threat to human health. To investigate the diversity of known and unknown viruses harbored by rodents in Guangdong (southern province of China), we conducted a comprehensive analysis of viral genomes through metagenomic sequencing of organs from 194 rodents.

pmc-10742488.title: Preliminary Investigation into the Prevalence of G6PD Deficiency in a Pediatric African American Population Using a Near-Patient Diagnostic Platform
pmc-10742488.creator: Van Leung-Pineda, Elizabeth P. Weinzierl, Beverly B. Rogers
pmc-10742488.description: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is prevalent in the African American population. We identified eighteen G6PD-deficient samples (9%) in a study of residual, de-identified whole blood specimens from 200 African American pediatric patients using a point-of-care instrument. This highlights the possibility of a rapid time to result for G6PD testing, which can be valuable in some clinical scenarios. 1.

pmc-11342478.creator: Mohammad Amin Nochian, Seyedhamidreza Mousavi, Hamed Khosravi, Mohammad Hasan Basirinezhad, Seyedmohammad Mirhosseini
pmc-11342478.description: BackgroundThe utilization of the Internet can lead to adverse outcomes in students’ lives. Prolonged Internet usage may result in academic failure, an elevated risk of musculoskeletal problems, and the emergence of issues impacting the lives of students and their peers.

pmc-11510390.description: Background/Objectives: Elevating ketone levels with therapeutic nutritional ketosis can help to metabolically manage disease processes associated with epilepsy, diabetes, obesity, cancer, and neurodegenerative disease. Nutritional ketosis can be achieved with various dieting strategies such as the classical ketogenic diet, the modified Atkins diet, caloric restriction, periodic fasting, or the consumption of exogenous ketogenic supplements such as medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs).

pmc-12660867.title: Influence of leadership on the adoption of circular and digital business models using PLS-SEM analysis
pmc-12660867.creator: Dalia Sanchez, Analí Sulca, Liz Pacheco-Pumaleque
pmc-12660867.description: In a business environment characterised by growing pressure towards sustainability and digital transformation, leadership emerges as a determining factor in the adoption of sustainable, technology-driven business models. This study analyses how leadership influences the adoption of circular business models and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in companies in Metropolitan Lima.

pmc-12990379.title: Metabolomics reveals multi-target bactericidal mechanisms of calcium-enhanced slightly acidic electrolyzed water (CSAEW) against Pseudomonas fluorescens and its synergistic preservation of fresh-cut lettuce
pmc-12990379.creator: Xinyu Li, Mengting Zhou, Wenman Wang, Jiating Huang, Mengli Kang, Hongfen Zhu, Xingquan Liu, Shanggui Deng, Jiangang Ling
pmc-12990379.description: This study demonstrated that slightly acidic electrolyzed water (CSAEW) effectively inactivates Pseudomonas fluorescens and preserves fresh-cut lettuce. CSAEW treatment induced severe membrane damage, causing potassium leakage (0.53 mmol/L), protein release (93.31 μg/mL), and elevated conductivity. SEM images showed collapsed membranes with pores. Metabolomics identified sn-Glycerol 3-phosphate and Ethenodeoxyadenosine as key reduced metabolites.

pmc-13059583.title: Effects of different planting patterns on potato rhizosphere soil microbial composition and yield
pmc-13059583.creator: Xiaoting Wang, Qingqing Hou, Fan Li, Liming Wang, Xiaoyan Zhang, Ruping Yang, Muhammad Aqeel, Chunhui Tang, Guangrong Chen
pmc-13059583.description: BackgroundPotato is a crucial dual-purpose crop, serving both as a staple food and vegetable in Northwest China. However, the prevalence of continuous monocropping has increasingly exacerbated continuous cropping obstacles in the region. While numerous studies have explored effective strategies for mitigating these obstacles, the impact of different cropping systems on potato yield and rhizosphere microbial communities remain insufficiently understood.

pmc-13400592.title: The adaptive learning taxonomy for responsible large language model integration in higher education
pmc-13400592.creator: Simon Baradziej, Adrianna Kochanska
pmc-13400592.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Large Language Models (LLMs) are being rapidly deployed in higher education, yet institutions lack integrated, theoretically grounded frameworks to guide responsible adoption. While meta-analytic evidence reports large positive effects on academic performance (g = 0.867; Wang and Fan 2025), emerging research reveals a “cognitive paradox”: performance gains may coincide with diminished metacognitive accuracy and self-regulation—a gap no existing framework comprehensively addresses across adaptation design, data governance, pedagogical targeting, and learner agency simultaneously.
